subject: geography

items.correct: Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs — balancing economic, social and environmental goals.
items.misconception: Sustainable development means stopping all economic growth.
items.random_wrong: Sustainable development means using only solar power.
items.why: Students treat sustainability as anti-development. The Brundtland definition is about balance and intergenerational equity — not zero growth or one specific technology.

items.correct: Growing plants in water with nutrients (no soil)
items.why: Correct answer: Growing plants in water with nutrients (no soil). “Growing plants underwater” sounds right because it borrows the language of the topic — but it fails this question. Re-read the notes on why.

items.q: Which is the MOST sustainable irrigation method?
items.why: It's Drip irrigation. “Flood irrigation” is the classic near-miss here; knowing why it's wrong is worth as much as knowing the right answer.

items.q: Approximately what PERCENTAGE of water can hydroponics save vs traditional field farming?
items.why: Exact answer: 90. Estimation gets you near it; only the anchored number survives the exam hall.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE Geography B (1GB0) specification; Resource Management
